about: The atlas's own taxonomy of the paper index. Every paper gets exactly one family (its main contribution); other families it touches go in 'also'. Families are grouped by where the memory lives (form) for methods, and by paper kind otherwise. Edit definitions here; the classification of each paper is in data/paper_families.json.

groups.name: Surveys
groups.def: Reviews, taxonomies and position papers on agent memory. Read these first.

families.name: Surveys and position papers
families.def: Reviews, taxonomies and position papers on agent memory.
families.test: Does it organize other work rather than propose a method?

axes.name: Taxonomy Basis
axes.def: The organizing principle the survey uses to structure agent memory research.

values.name: Architecture-Based
values.def: Organizes memory by system or representational structure (forms, storage, modules, substrates).

values.name: Process/Stage-Based
values.def: Organizes memory by operations or evolutionary stages over time (write-manage-read, storage-reflection-experience, six operations).

values.name: Cognitive/Neuroscience-Based
values.def: Organizes memory by analogy to human or biological memory categories and brain function.

values.name: Broader System Layer
values.def: Treats memory as one layer within a larger system (harness, multi-agent, tools, vision, video) rather than the sole focus.

axes.name: Evidence Base
axes.def: What kind of support the paper offers for its claims.

values.name: Conceptual Only
values.def: Presents a taxonomy or argument without new benchmarks or experiments.

values.name: Benchmark Survey
values.def: Reviews and analyzes existing benchmarks or evaluation practices without running new experiments.

values.name: Empirical Analysis
values.def: Runs its own experiments or comparisons across methods or benchmarks.

values.name: Position/Argument
values.def: Makes a normative or risk-based argument rather than presenting a neutral taxonomy.

groups.name: Token-level memory
groups.def: Memory is text or records outside the model that are read back into its context.

families.name: Working-context management
families.def: Shrinks, folds, branches or prunes the running context inside one long task. No store that outlives the task.
families.test: Does the memory disappear when the task ends, and is the point to fit a long trajectory into the window?

axes.name: Context representation
axes.def: The form the retained working context takes.

values.name: Single evolving summary
values.def: One flowing text state, memo, or report that is overwritten or extended over time.

values.name: Structured multi-field
values.def: Several explicit named memory fields or types held alongside each other (e.g. folded history plus UI state, or episodic/working/tool).

values.name: Tree/graph structure
values.def: An explicit tree, graph, or plan data structure with nodes and edges.

values.name: Direct raw-context edit
values.def: No separate memory object; operates directly on the token sequence via insertion, deletion, eviction, or search over raw content.

values.name: Not stated
values.def: No representation is given in the available text.

axes.name: Management scope
axes.def: What kind of content the context operation targets.

values.name: Agent's own trajectory
values.def: The agent's own action-observation/interaction history accumulated across steps.

values.name: Tool/environment context
values.def: External tool, API, MCP-server definitions, or workspace artefacts shared across roles.

values.name: Search/reasoning state
values.def: Intermediate search, planning, or belief state built during multi-step reasoning.

values.name: Long input document
values.def: A single long given text/narrative/conversation being read, not the agent's own generated trajectory.

values.name: Not stated
values.def: No scope is given in the available text.

families.name: Flat retrieval store
families.def: Persistent records (turns, chunks, facts, summaries) retrieved by similarity or keywords; items are not linked to each other.
families.test: Is there a store of records whose items have no edges or levels between them?

axes.name: Retrieval strategy
axes.def: How a query finds the right stored items.

values.name: Single-pass similarity
values.def: One-shot dense/keyword top-k lookup against the store.

values.name: Adaptive dual-path
values.def: Switches or combines two or more retrieval routes based on a signal (familiarity, intent, surface vs. latent match).

values.name: Structured, non-similarity
values.def: Bypasses vector/keyword similarity via typed lookup, scoring policy, access control, or explicit structure.

values.name: Learned retrieval policy
values.def: Retrieval or reranking is itself trained (RL, SFT, or refined from interaction experience).

values.name: Not stated
values.def: No retrieval mechanism is given in the available text.

axes.name: Memory unit type
axes.def: The granularity/shape of what is stored per item.

values.name: Raw/summarized turns
values.def: Whole dialogue turns, memos, or lightly summarized interaction history.

values.name: Extracted atomic facts
values.def: Discrete distilled facts, beliefs, or relations pulled out of interactions.

values.name: Typed multi-category
values.def: Multiple explicit memory types or fields held side by side (e.g. episodic/semantic/procedural, dual-brain, paired units).

values.name: Exemplar/trajectory records
values.def: Whole action or dialogue trajectories/exemplars stored intact for reuse.

values.name: Not stated
values.def: No memory content/unit is given in the available text.

families.name: Graph and linked store
families.def: Records connected by edges: knowledge graphs, entity or temporal graphs, linked notes. Retrieval or update uses the links.
families.test: Are items connected, and does the method rely on those connections?

axes.name: Node/edge unit
axes.def: What the graph's nodes and edges represent.

values.name: Entity-relation KG
values.def: Nodes are entities and edges are relations, as in a classic knowledge graph.

values.name: Event/proposition
values.def: Nodes are events, episodes, or extracted propositions rather than bare entities.

values.name: Hyperedge
values.def: Edges are hyperedges connecting three or more nodes to capture n-ary or grouped relations.

values.name: Multi-view/heterogeneous
values.def: Memory is represented across several parallel graph types or node roles at once.

values.name: Text-unit graph
values.def: Nodes are raw text spans such as sentences, utterances, or notes linked to each other.

values.name: Not stated
values.def: The text gives no information about what nodes and edges represent.

axes.name: Retrieval read mechanism
axes.def: How the graph is traversed or queried to answer a request.

values.name: Structural traversal
values.def: Retrieval walks or scores the graph structure itself, e.g. multi-hop paths, PageRank, or trees.

values.name: Trained retriever/policy
values.def: A learned model or an RL/SFT-trained policy performs or guides retrieval.

values.name: Agentic iterative
values.def: An LLM agent iteratively decides retrieval actions or tool calls over the graph.

values.name: Multi-signal hybrid
values.def: Retrieval fuses multiple routes or signals such as similarity, structure, and recency.

values.name: Similarity search
values.def: Retrieval is primarily embedding-based nearest-neighbor search, possibly enriched with extra features.

values.name: Not stated
values.def: The text gives no information about the retrieval mechanism.

families.name: Hierarchical and tiered store
families.def: Records at several levels of abstraction (tree, clusters, summaries over details) or in tiers that items move between (short-term, long-term, archive).
families.test: Are there levels or tiers, and is moving between them part of the method?

axes.name: Consolidation Trigger
axes.def: What causes memory to be built, promoted, or reorganized across levels.

values.name: Continuous / Every-Turn
values.def: Memory is processed and reorganized on every interaction, with no separate gating condition.

values.name: Event-Triggered
values.def: Consolidation fires only when a specific condition is met, such as recurrence, capacity limits, or task completion.

values.name: Scheduled / Periodic
values.def: Consolidation runs on a fixed periodic or offline (sleep-time) schedule decoupled from individual interactions.

values.name: Learned Policy
values.def: A trained RL or SFT policy decides when and what to consolidate or retrieve.

values.name: Not Stated
values.def: The paper gives no information about the consolidation trigger.

axes.name: Retrieval Traversal
axes.def: How the system navigates the hierarchy to answer a query at inference time.

values.name: Top-Down Index Routing
values.def: Retrieval follows explicit indices or pointers from coarse to fine levels, avoiding exhaustive similarity search.

values.name: Similarity + Aggregation
values.def: Vector similarity search is combined with hierarchy-aware scoring or aggregation of related items.

values.name: Agentic Exploration
values.def: An LLM or trained agent actively and iteratively decides what to fetch, reason over, or explore next.

values.name: Single-Pass Regeneration
values.def: There is no separate retrieval step; memory is directly regenerated or merged into the next response.

values.name: Not Stated
values.def: The paper gives no information about retrieval traversal.

families.name: Experience and skill memory
families.def: Distills reusable insights, workflows, strategies, tools or code from past trajectories so the agent acts better on later tasks. Weights stay frozen.
families.test: Is what is stored lessons or procedures learned from doing tasks, rather than facts about the world or the user?

axes.name: Memory Content Type
axes.def: What kind of artifact the system stores and reuses as its memory.

values.name: Episodic Cases
values.def: Raw or lightly processed episodic trajectories or cases from past interactions.

values.name: Distilled Insight
values.def: Distilled natural-language insights, strategies, principles, or beliefs abstracted from experience.

values.name: Procedural Skill
values.def: Reusable executable skills, workflows, tools, APIs, or documentation.

values.name: System Architecture
values.def: The memory system or agent architecture/code itself is the evolving artifact.

axes.name: Update Mechanism
axes.def: How the memory content is decided, accepted, or improved over time.

values.name: Gated by Score
values.def: An update is accepted only after passing an explicit validation, risk, or utility gate.

values.name: RL Optimized
values.def: Updates or selection are driven by a reinforcement-learning or bandit reward signal.

values.name: Free-form Reflection
values.def: Updates come from unstructured self-reflection, distillation, or accumulation without formal gating or RL.

values.name: Search Evolved
values.def: Updates come from population-based or iterative search/evolution over candidate designs.

families.name: Multimodal and embodied store
families.def: Stores and retrieves non-text observations (video, images, screens, 3D or spatial maps) as the main contribution.
families.test: Is handling a non-text modality the paper's main point?

axes.name: What is stored
axes.def: The form the memory actually holds in the system.

values.name: Raw frames/keyframes
values.def: Memory keeps literal video frames, keyframes, or imagined images.

values.name: Learned latent tokens
values.def: Memory is a compressed, opaque neural embedding or token bank produced by a trained encoder.

values.name: Structured symbolic memory
values.def: Memory is human-interpretable structure: graphs, entities, events, text summaries, or maps.

values.name: External retrieval corpus
values.def: Memory is a separate indexed database of videos/clips queried like a search index.

values.name: Not stated
values.def: The abstract does not specify the concrete memory representation.

axes.name: How memory is used
axes.def: The mechanism by which memory is written, selected, or read at inference time.

values.name: Trained fusion/attention
values.def: Memory read or write is a trained, model-internal step (attention, latent fusion, RL/SFT policy) with no explicit query loop.

values.name: Agentic iterative retrieval
values.def: An LLM/VLM agent actively decides what to query, store, verify, or backtrack across memory through reasoning.

values.name: Relevance-based retrieval
values.def: Memory items are selected by a relevance criterion (semantic similarity, prompt match, geometric overlap) without agentic iteration or joint training.

values.name: Fixed rule/compression
values.def: A deterministic, training-free algorithm compresses or extracts memory with no learning, agent, or query step.

values.name: Not stated
values.def: The abstract does not specify the access mechanism.

groups.name: Parametric memory
groups.def: Memory is written into model weights.

families.name: Knowledge editing
families.def: Targeted weight updates that insert, change or delete specific facts.
families.test: Does it change particular facts in a trained model by editing its weights?

axes.name: Edit mechanism
axes.def: How the weight update itself is computed and applied.

values.name: Null-space projection
values.def: Projects edit perturbations onto a null space to avoid disrupting other knowledge.

values.name: Hypernetwork prediction
values.def: A trained hypernetwork predicts the weight update for a given fact.

values.name: LoRA adapter mixture
values.def: Edits are stored as a mixture of LoRA adapters.

values.name: Dual-memory router
values.def: A router selects between a frozen main memory and an edited side memory.

values.name: Perturbation analysis
values.def: No new editing mechanism; studies side effects of existing edit methods.

axes.name: Primary concern
axes.def: The main property the paper optimizes or evaluates.

values.name: Locality preservation
values.def: Focuses on keeping unrelated knowledge intact during editing.

values.name: Lifelong stability
values.def: Focuses on stability across many sequential edits over time.

values.name: Scalability
values.def: Focuses on making editing fast and scalable to many facts.

values.name: Generalization
values.def: Focuses on edits generalizing consistently to paraphrases of the query.

values.name: Side-effect analysis
values.def: Focuses on characterizing unintended perturbations caused by editing.

families.name: Internalizing experience
families.def: Fine-tunes or reinforces the agent on trajectories (its own or collected) so that skills or knowledge end up in the weights.
families.test: Is the memory the effect of training the agent model on experience?

axes.name: Experience source
axes.def: Where the training data that gets internalized comes from.

values.name: Self-generated rollouts
values.def: Comes from the agent's own real-time interaction, tool use, or trial-and-error.

values.name: Synthetic model-generated
values.def: Comes from a learned model that synthesizes rollouts or curricula.

values.name: Expert corpus/pretraining
values.def: Comes from a fixed expert or persona corpus used for pretraining/fine-tuning.

values.name: Continual task stream
values.def: Comes from a stream of tasks arriving sequentially over time.

axes.name: Internalization mechanism
axes.def: The mechanism that turns experience into a weight update.

values.name: Hindsight reflection
values.def: Extracts natural-language lessons or skills from trajectories, then trains on them.

values.name: Dual-pathway architecture
values.def: Splits learning across two explicit fast/slow or fast/meta parameter pathways.

values.name: Curriculum/synthetic rollout
values.def: Generates synthetic tasks or transitions to expand training rollouts.

values.name: Selective parameter targeting
values.def: Restricts updates to selected parameters or samples to limit forgetting.

values.name: Direct fine-tune
values.def: Standard SFT or RL fine-tuning on collected data, no extra structure.

families.name: Parametric memory module
families.def: A dedicated trainable memory component attached to the model: memory layers, adapters, memory decoders, memory tokens learned as parameters.
families.test: Is there a separate set of parameters whose job is to hold memory?

axes.name: Memory unit type
axes.def: What kind of structure holds the stored information.

values.name: Sparse lookup slots
values.def: Fixed addressable slots (N-gram, product-key, or sparse layer) looked up by content.

values.name: Separate trainable submodel
values.def: A distinct auxiliary network (decoder, MLP, bank) separate from the lookup-table paradigm.

values.name: Adapter/LoRA memory
values.def: LoRA-style adapters serve as the memory-carrying parameters.

values.name: Token as memory unit
values.def: A discrete trainable token indexes and steers one piece of knowledge or a procedure.

values.name: Not stated
values.def: Memory unit type is not stated.

axes.name: Primary goal
axes.def: What the memory module is mainly built to achieve.

values.name: Factual knowledge storage
values.def: Aimed at storing or injecting factual/world knowledge.

values.name: Procedural skill storage
values.def: Aimed at storing reusable task procedures, tools, or execution strategies.

values.name: Capacity/efficiency architecture
values.def: Aimed at scaling model capacity or efficiency as an architecture contribution.

values.name: On-device personalization
values.def: Aimed at private, on-device personalized memory.

values.name: Not stated
values.def: Primary goal is not stated.

groups.name: Latent memory
groups.def: Memory is hidden states, key-value caches or vectors the model consumes internally, not readable text.

families.name: KV cache compression and reuse
families.def: Selects, evicts, merges, quantizes or reuses attention key-value states to keep long contexts affordable.
families.test: Is the object being managed the KV cache?

axes.name: Decision Driver
axes.def: What determines which KV entries are kept, evicted, or retrieved.

values.name: Trained Selector
values.def: A component is trained (SFT/RL/pretraining) to decide what KV content to keep or route.

values.name: Fixed Heuristic
values.def: A static, hand-designed scoring rule (importance, position, frequency) picks what to keep, no training.

values.name: Structural Reuse
values.def: Training-free reuse of hierarchical or block-structured memory units looked up by relevance.

values.name: System Scheduling
values.def: Memory is pooled, paged, or scheduled across requests/instances with no content-level importance decision.

axes.name: Target Scope
axes.def: The setting in which the KV mechanism is applied.

values.name: Single-Sequence LM
values.def: Operates within one model's decoding of a single long text sequence.

values.name: RAG Context
values.def: Targets the concatenated retrieved-passage context typical of retrieval-augmented generation.

values.name: Video
values.def: Applied to video generation or streaming video understanding models.

values.name: Multi-Request Serving
values.def: Manages KV cache across many concurrent requests or serving instances.

families.name: Memory-augmented architecture
families.def: Changes the model architecture so it carries a memory state across segments: recurrent memory, external attention memory, test-time-updated memory.
families.test: Is the contribution a new layer or architecture with a built-in memory state?

axes.name: Memory Storage Form
axes.def: The literal form the persistent memory state takes.

values.name: Vector State
values.def: A single fixed-size matrix/vector (or model weights) holds compressed past information.

values.name: Token/Slot Memory
values.def: A discrete set of memory tokens, slots, or modules is attended to via cross-attention.

values.name: Not Stated
values.def: Title only; storage form not given.

axes.name: Update Mechanism
axes.def: How the memory content is written or updated over time.

values.name: Test-Time Optimization
values.def: Memory is updated online at inference via gradient descent, a delta rule, or a learned local update rule.

values.name: Gated Forward Write
values.def: Memory is written via a learned gate/router in a single forward pass, no test-time gradients.

values.name: Fixed Attention Accumulation
values.def: Memory content accumulates via standard trained cross-/self-attention, no explicit separate write step.

values.name: Not Stated
values.def: Title only; update mechanism not given.

families.name: Latent memory generation
families.def: The model writes compact latent tokens or vectors (gist tokens, soft thoughts, compressed context) that stand in for longer text.
families.test: Does the model produce latent vectors meant to be read back instead of text?

axes.name: Production Mechanism
axes.def: How the latent representation is generated.

values.name: Test-Time Optimization
values.def: A per-sample optimization loop at inference writes the latent, nothing persists across tasks.

values.name: Trained Encoder
values.def: A dedicated encoder/autoencoder network, trained ahead of time, produces the latent from input context.

values.name: Generative Latent Reasoning
values.def: Latent tokens are produced on-the-fly, interleaved with the model's own reasoning or decoding.

values.name: Draft & Retrieve
values.def: A light model builds a global latent memory and drafts clues that steer a separate retriever/answerer.

values.name: Not Stated
values.def: Title only; production mechanism not given.

axes.name: Primary Use
axes.def: What the generated latent is ultimately used for.

values.name: Context Compression
values.def: Latent stands in for a long text context so it can be conditioned on cheaply.

values.name: Reasoning Augmentation
values.def: Latent stands in for explicit chain-of-thought or visual reasoning steps.

values.name: Retrieval Support
values.def: Latent guides retrieval or judges the reliability of retrieved content in a RAG pipeline.

values.name: Not Stated
values.def: Title only; use not given.

families.name: Latent memory pool
families.def: A persistent bank of latent vectors outside the forward pass that is retrieved from and updated over time.
families.test: Is there a long-lived store of hidden-state vectors, written and read across inputs?

axes.name: Pool Content
axes.def: What kind of information the persistent latent pool stores.

values.name: Hidden-State Latent
values.def: The pool holds compressed hidden-state or embedding vectors representing past knowledge.

values.name: Frozen Encoded Tokens
values.def: The pool caches representations produced by a frozen backbone acting purely as an encoder.

values.name: Amortized Adaptation Params
values.def: The pool stores learned parameters representing amortized adaptation to past contexts.

values.name: Episodic Trajectories
values.def: The pool stores discrete past episodes/experiences for later recall.

axes.name: Access Mechanism
axes.def: How stored content is retrieved or integrated at use time.

values.name: Direct Integration
values.def: Pool content is fed straight into the backbone's own attention/input layer, no separate retriever module.

values.name: Co-Trained Retriever
values.def: A distinct retriever module, trained alongside the pool, dynamically fetches relevant content.

values.name: Amortization Lookup
values.def: Stored adaptation parameters are applied directly rather than retrieved by similarity.

values.name: RL Policy Recall
values.def: A reinforcement-learned policy decides when and what episodic memory to recall.

groups.name: Benchmarks
groups.def: Papers whose main contribution is an evaluation.

families.name: Conversational long-term memory
families.def: Questions over long multi-session dialogues or user histories: recall, temporal reasoning, knowledge update, personalization.
families.test: Is the input a long conversation or user history and the task answering about it?

axes.name: Primary Probe Target
axes.def: What the QA pairs are designed to test about the user or conversation.

values.name: Factual/Event Recall
values.def: Straightforward extraction of facts or events stated in the dialogue.

values.name: Implicit Latent State
values.def: Retention and application of unqueried constraints such as goals, values or subjective states.

values.name: Evolving User Profile
values.def: Tracking how a user's traits, preferences or persona change and personalizing accordingly.

values.name: Memory Architecture Comparison
values.def: Comparing or proposing memory system designs rather than a specific persona or fact type.

axes.name: Temporal Dynamics Emphasis
axes.def: Whether the benchmark centers on information changing/updating over time or on static comprehension.

values.name: Temporal/Update Focus
values.def: Explicitly probes temporal reasoning, knowledge updates or state evolution across sessions.

values.name: Static Comprehension Focus
values.def: Treats the conversation as a fixed record to comprehend, without a dedicated update/temporal test.

families.name: Agent tasks that need memory
families.def: Interactive or long-horizon tasks (web, GUI, embodied, games, tools) where the agent must remember across steps or episodes.
families.test: Does the agent act in an environment and memory is needed to succeed?

axes.name: Interaction Domain
axes.def: The kind of environment the agent acts in.

values.name: Web Browsing
values.def: Tasks performed on websites via a browser interface.

values.name: GUI/OS Computer Use
values.def: Mobile or desktop GUI and operating-system level interaction.

values.name: Embodied Household
values.def: Simulated physical or embodied navigation and manipulation tasks.

values.name: Text/Tool/Coding
values.def: Text-based games, API calls, or code-execution tool environments.

values.name: Cross-Domain Framework
values.def: A general platform or gym spanning multiple task domains rather than one fixed environment.

axes.name: Memory Demand Type
axes.def: What kind of memory the benchmark specifically stresses, if any.

values.name: Cross-Session Experience Reuse
values.def: Agent must distill experience in one session/episode and reuse it in later, separate ones.

values.name: Long-Horizon Within-Episode Tracking
values.def: A single continuous long trajectory requires tracking state and history throughout.

values.name: Multi-Competency Diagnostic
values.def: Explicitly decomposes memory into several named competencies with dedicated metrics.

values.name: General Capability, No Memory Focus
values.def: A standard agent benchmark not centered on memory, used here as an environment/baseline.

families.name: Multimodal memory evaluation
families.def: Memory over video, images or embodied observations.
families.test: Is the remembered input mainly non-text?

axes.name: Modality Domain
axes.def: The kind of multimodal content and setting the memory is evaluated over.

values.name: Video World-Model Generation
values.def: Memory of a generative video world model that must stay internally consistent.

values.name: Egocentric Streaming Life-Log
values.def: Continuous first-person video/audio/text streams of daily life.

values.name: Robotic Manipulation
values.def: Physical or simulated robot manipulation trajectories.

values.name: Personal Multimodal History
values.def: A user's accumulated personal images, videos, emails or conversation history.

values.name: Long Video QA (General)
values.def: General-domain long videos (movies, web videos) with question answering, not personal or streaming.

axes.name: Contribution Type
axes.def: Whether the paper proposes a new memory module, a new evaluation metric, or just a fixed QA benchmark.

values.name: Proposes Memory Module
values.def: Introduces a new memory-bearing model/policy architecture alongside the benchmark.

values.name: Novel Metric Framework
values.def: Introduces new scoring dimensions or metrics without proposing a new memory architecture.

values.name: Fixed QA Benchmark
values.def: Standard multiple-choice or QA evaluation with conventional accuracy metrics.

families.name: Other memory evaluation
families.def: Probes of memory abilities that are neither conversations nor agent tasks: long-context retrieval, knowledge editing, memory security.
families.test: Everything else that is mainly an evaluation.

axes.name: Probe Focus
axes.def: What memory-related capability or system aspect is being probed.

values.name: Long-Context Retrieval/Reasoning
values.def: How well models retrieve or reason over long raw text contexts, independent of an agent framework.

values.name: Memory System Architecture Comparison
values.def: Compares or characterizes specific memory-system implementations (structures, harnesses, providers).

values.name: Memory Reliability/Learning Dynamics
values.def: How memory quality degrades or improves through hallucination, consolidation, or continual feedback.

values.name: Personalized Multi-Hop Reasoning
values.def: Reasoning across multiple pieces of personalized user information to answer a query.

axes.name: Evaluation Vehicle
axes.def: How the probe is operationalized methodologically.

values.name: Needle-in-Haystack Variant
values.def: A planted-fact retrieval task designed to remove literal-matching shortcuts.

values.name: Atomic Task Suite
values.def: Automatically generated elementary memory operations (search, recall, edit, compare) plus composites.

values.name: Curated MCQ over Long Documents
values.def: Human-curated multiple-choice questions over long natural documents.

values.name: Leaderboard Platform
values.def: An open, ongoing scoring platform where external memory systems are submitted and ranked.

values.name: Empirical Systems Study
values.def: Controlled experiments measuring existing memory systems' behavior, cost, or failure modes.

groups.name: Other entries
groups.def: Entries that are not a method or a benchmark.

families.name: Memory security and privacy
families.def: Attacks on memory (poisoning, injection, extraction), defenses, and privacy of what memory keeps about users.
families.test: Is the paper about threats to memory or protecting what it stores?

axes.name: Paper role
axes.def: Whether the paper attacks, defends, benchmarks, or probes memory.

values.name: Attack method
values.def: Proposes a new attack technique against agent memory.

values.name: Defense mechanism
values.def: Proposes a mechanism to defend or protect memory.

values.name: Benchmark/taxonomy
values.def: Builds a benchmark or taxonomy for evaluating memory attacks/integrity.

values.name: Vulnerability probe
values.def: Provides runnable probes demonstrating a specific vulnerability.

axes.name: Threat focus
axes.def: Which class of harm to memory the paper centers on.

values.name: Privacy leakage
values.def: Centers on exposure of private user/agent information.

values.name: Poisoning/write attacks
values.def: Centers on adversarial or forged writes corrupting memory.

values.name: Integrity benchmarking
values.def: Centers on general benchmarking of memory integrity, not one threat class.

families.name: Products and frameworks
families.def: Software memory layers, services and frameworks, open or closed source, described by their project rather than a paper.
families.test: Is the entry a product or code project?

axes.name: Primary mechanism
axes.def: The main technical mechanism each product foregrounds as its distinguishing feature.

values.name: Retrieval technique
values.def: Distinguished mainly by its search/indexing method (lexical, dense, hybrid, or graph traversal).

values.name: Lifecycle & temporal
values.def: Distinguished mainly by how memories age, decay, are forgotten, versioned, or superseded over time.

values.name: Trust & governance
values.def: Distinguished mainly by provenance, audit trails, permissions, encryption, or human-gated writes.

values.name: Coordination & sharing
values.def: Distinguished mainly by sharing or coordinating memory across a fleet or team of agents.

values.name: Not stated
values.def: No distinguishing mechanism is described in the available text.

axes.name: Access & runtime mode
axes.def: How the memory system is built and reached at runtime.

values.name: MCP server
values.def: Exposed to agents primarily as a Model Context Protocol server/tool set.

values.name: Local CLI/binary
values.def: A local-first CLI, binary, or embedded library without MCP as the stated interface.

values.name: Hosted API/service
values.def: A hosted, cloud, or managed API/SaaS product.

values.name: Framework or spec
values.def: A general lifecycle framework, operating system, or operation-language specification, not one runnable store.

values.name: Not stated
values.def: No access or runtime mode is described in the available text.

families.name: Cognitive science and neuroscience
families.def: Studies of human or animal memory cited for inspiration.
families.test: Is the subject biological memory?

axes.name: Memory process
axes.def: Which stage of memory the study addresses.

values.name: Encoding/representation
values.def: How memories are encoded or represented in neural populations/state spaces.

values.name: Consolidation
values.def: How memories are consolidated or constructed over time.

values.name: Retrieval
values.def: How memories are retrieved or recalled.

values.name: Forgetting/updating
values.def: How memories are forgotten, distorted, or updated.

axes.name: Methodology
axes.def: The kind of evidence or model used.

values.name: Computational model
values.def: Uses a computational or simulation model to explain the phenomenon.

values.name: Neural recording/empirical
values.def: Uses neural recordings or brain-circuit evidence.

values.name: Behavioral/cognitive
values.def: Uses behavioral or cognitive-level evidence.

families.name: Other
families.def: Tutorials, articles and workshops about memory.
families.test: A memory-related entry that is not a method, benchmark, survey, product or cogsci study.

axes.name: Content Type
axes.def: The delivery format of the item.

values.name: Practical Guide
values.def: A blog post, article or guide explaining a memory-related topic.

values.name: Structured Tutorial
values.def: A conference tutorial or workshop session with organized teaching content.

values.name: Conference Venue
values.def: A listing for a conference or venue, not itself content about memory.

axes.name: Topic Focus
axes.def: What aspect of agent memory the item's title centers on.

values.name: Architecture Choice
values.def: Focuses on selecting or designing a memory architecture.

values.name: Optimization/Efficiency
values.def: Focuses on optimizing memory for cost or performance.

values.name: Agent Workflow/Context
values.def: Places memory within the broader agent workflow of tools, actions and context.

values.name: General Overview
values.def: A general introduction or comprehensive overview of memory topics.

values.name: Not Stated
values.def: The title gives no indication of a specific memory topic.

families.name: Not about memory
families.def: General agent, tool-use or unrelated papers that the source lists include but that do not study memory. Kept in the data so a re-import does not bring them back, never shown.
families.test: Would the paper still make its point with memory removed?

families.name: Theory and analysis
families.def: Analyses, measurements and theoretical results about memory that propose neither a method nor a benchmark. Not shown for now.
families.test: Is the contribution a finding or a proof rather than a system or an evaluation?
examples: How Much Do Language Models Memorize?

functions.name: Factual
functions.def: facts about the world or the user

functions.name: Experiential
functions.def: lessons, skills and procedures from past tasks

learning.name: Does not learn
learning.def: Stores new records, but how it writes and reads never changes: fixed rules or a prompted LLM.

learning.name: Learns from experience, no training
learning.def: Gets better from past tasks without weight updates: stored reflections, insights, skills or workflows, or edits to its own prompts, tools or harness.

learning.name: Supervised training
learning.def: A model is fine-tuned on labelled or imitation data to manage memory or to hold it.

learning.name: Reinforcement learning
learning.def: A memory policy or the agent is trained with rewards from task outcomes.

learning.name: Trained with the model
learning.def: The memory is a component learned during model (pre)training or end-to-end training, not a policy for memory operations, e.g. memory layers, recurrent memory, KV selection learned offline.

token|factual.text: Facts about users and the world, kept as text records that are retrieved back into the prompt.

token|experiential.text: Lessons, skills and workflows from past tasks, kept as text the agent reads before acting.

token|working.text: The running task context itself, condensed, folded or paged so a long task fits the window.

parametric|factual.text: Facts written into model weights: targeted edits, memory layers, trained memory modules.

parametric|experiential.text: Skills learned into the weights by training the agent on trajectories.

parametric|working.text: Task state held in the weights during a single task.
parametric|working.note: No paper in the index. Weight updates are slow and persistent, while task state is short-lived. Test-time memory updates by gradient steps (Titans, GradMem) are placed under Latent · Working, since that state is discarded after the input.

latent|factual.text: Facts kept as hidden-state vectors or a latent pool the model attends to.

latent|experiential.note: Only two papers in the index.

latent|working.text: The current context held as KV cache, recurrent state or compressed latent tokens.

token|unspecified.text: Text-record memory whose purpose the source does not state.

parametric|unspecified.text: Weight-based memory whose purpose the source does not state.

latent|unspecified.text: Latent memory whose purpose the source does not state.
